terms.definition: One named number a scale can drive, such as reach or motion. Unset, it follows the base scale raised to an exponent; an override replaces it.
A named size and shape a datapack declares for an entity, with optional part factors, hurt regions and threshold overrides. Stature ships none.
A named set of part groups and the model paths each group covers, loaded from a datapack. The built-in stature:humanoid rig is the fallback.
A per-axis multiplier on one model part, or on every part a rig group covers. It changes the silhouette, not the entity's box, unless a frame sets hitbox_from_parts.
One of the two scale edges that decide when the micro and macro mechanics run. A frame may move either edge for its entities.
An entity whose uniform scale is below its micro threshold. Micro entities climb walls and pass through bars, fences and bamboo when those flags are on.
An entity whose uniform scale is above its macro threshold. Macro entities trample fragile blocks, compress under low ceilings and make seismic footsteps when those flags are on.
A part of a frame's body that takes a different damage multiplier. A region names a rig group, uses that group's fractional box and carries a tag for other mods.
The range the game's minecraft:scale attribute accepts, 0.0625 to 16. A size outside it needs dangerous mode.
A scale outside the game's envelope. A dangerous set keeps the box at the nearest bound and draws the model at the requested size.
The stature:scale entity-selector option, which filters living entities by their uniform scale using vanilla range syntax, such as 0.5..2.
The server config family for a Stature-applied channel: an on/off flag, a strength multiplier and min/max clamps. Per-entity overrides and frames sit on top of it.
Multiplying the count of loot-table stacks from a scaled entity. Only stackable items scale; uniques are never duplicated and equipment is untouched.
